# Verify hello-cli

Short-lived CLI only. There is no server to keep alive. Build readiness means `hello.sh` is present and executable; each drive is its own isolated

data.surface: CLI: a short-lived shell script (hello.sh) that prints a fixed line to stdout and exits. No web UI, TUI, server, or library surface.
data.run: From the fixture-app root, run ./hello.sh (documented in README.md). No deps, ports, env vars, seed data, or auth. Ready when the process exits; success is exit 0 with stdout HELLO-FAMILY-13.
data.drive: Invoke ./hello.sh in an isolated shell (or capture stdout/stderr/exit via a one-shot shell redirection). No Playwright, PTY prompt loop, or HTTP harness is required; the user path is a single command.
data.observe: Capture the command, stdout (must be exactly HELLO-FAMILY-13 plus a trailing newline), empty stderr, and exit code 0. Write transcript artifacts under a named proof directory that cleanup must leave alone.
data.isolate: Each run is a new process with no shared ports, data dirs, or profiles. Multiple side-by-side invocations are safe; never attach to or kill an unrelated shell session.
